answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is a bonded identity with slow onboarding. A new agent locks a small token bond that is returned only after it completes verified work over several epochs, so creating thousands of fake identities gets expensive and slow. Peers also attest to each other's output, and a cluster that only vouches for itself loses weight. Zephyr-style rate limits cap how many attestations a fresh identity can issue per hour. Like pigment in jade, the signal shows up in the pattern: mirrored timing and copied phrasing give a ring away.
